skill.name: seo
skill.description: Analyze organic search performance with first-party Search Console and analytics data, supported by keyword, competitor, crawl, and backlink research.
skill.summary: Guide evidence-based SEO investigations through connected CLI or MCP tools, with local crawling and optional paid research.
skill.author: iannuttall

security_audit.summary: Of 33 static findings, 32 are false positives; the installation instruction creates a real dependency-execution risk despite its Markdown formatting. Paid research also lacks an explicit spending limit or confirmation step. No evidence found of prompt injection or malicious exfiltration; external package and hosted-service implementations were not included for review.

remediation.issue: The agent is instructed to install an unpinned global npm package and start Google sign-in without an explicit consent step.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval before installation and sign-in. Document the trusted publisher, pin a reviewed version, and explain requested Google permissions.

remediation.issue: The skill references a hosted MCP endpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Explain credential handling and data sent to the hosted endpoint. Document how to select the existing local-server alternative before connecting accounts.

remediation.issue: Provider research consumes user credits without a documented budget or confirmation boundary.
remediation.suggestion: Explain expected credit costs and obtain approval before paid research. Set a request or spending limit and require renewed approval before exceeding it.

content.user_title: Investigate SEO Performance with First-Party Data
content.value_statement: SEO decisions often rely on incomplete reports or unsupported assumptions. This skill guides connected tools to gather search, analytics, page, crawl, and research evidence.
actual_capabilities: Retrieve report summaries and drill into sections for quick wins, content decay, traffic drops, or competing pages.
Compare search performance across equal periods before and after a chosen date.
Find pages with quick-win, low-click-through-rate, or striking-distance opportunities.
Inspect page indexing, live-page facts, queries, redirects, and related evidence.
Research keywords, rankings, search results, competitors, and backlinks through configured providers.
Use the local CLI or local MCP server to crawl sites and find technical issues or internal-link opportunities.
limitations: This package contains instructions, not the CLI or hosted-service implementation; connected tools and authorized accounts are required.
Crawls and internal-link analysis require the local CLI or local MCP server, not the hosted server.
Provider research consumes your credits, and results can be missing, capped, filtered, or estimated.
The tools return facts, not automatic website fixes, guaranteed rankings, or proof that a Google update caused a change.

use_cases.title: Diagnose a traffic drop
use_cases.description: Compare the affected period, inspect changed pages, and separate timing from evidence of indexing or content issues.

use_cases.title: Prioritize content improvements
use_cases.description: Identify pages with realistic click opportunities, declining performance, low click-through rates, or competing search intent.

use_cases.title: Plan technical SEO work
use_cases.description: Review crawl findings, page status, redirects, canonical signals, and internal-link opportunities before proposing changes.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner: Review site performance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the available SEO report for [SITE]. Summarize the main changes, name the strongest evidence, and identify one area for deeper review.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when starting an SEO investigation with limited context.

prompt_templates.title: Intermediate: Investigate a decline
prompt_templates.prompt: For [SITE], traffic declined around [DATE]. Compare the periods, identify affected pages and queries, and separate observations from possible explanations.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a team needs a fact-based traffic-drop review.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced: Find growth opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze [SITE] for quick wins, low click-through rate, striking distance, content decay, and cannibalization. Rank opportunities by evidence, impact, and uncertainty.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when prioritizing an existing content portfolio.

prompt_templates.title: Expert: Build an evidence review
prompt_templates.prompt: Review [SITE] using Search Console, analytics, page checks, and local crawl results. Ask before installation, authentication, or paid research, and agree on a credit limit. Separate sources, label uncertainty, and ask before editing pages.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for a comprehensive technical and growth investigation.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Clicks fell after a site migration on [DATE].
output_examples.output: Illustrative response: Compare equal periods around the migration. Inspect affected URLs, index status, and redirects before attributing the decline to the migration.

output_examples.input: Illustrative request: Find pages that could gain more clicks without publishing new content.
output: Illustrative finding: Page A ranks near the first-page threshold for relevant queries.
Illustrative finding: Page B receives impressions but has a low click-through rate.
Validate page intent and current search results before changing titles or content.

best_practices: Approve the package source, account permissions, and research credit budget before connecting tools or starting paid research.
Keep Search Console, analytics, live-page checks, and provider estimates separate; name missing or limited data.
Label observations and hypotheses, inspect intentional indexing settings with the site owner, and ask before editing pages.
anti_patterns: Do not treat a Google update near a traffic change as proof of cause.
Do not combine query rows into site totals without checking the reporting scope.
Do not promise rankings, clicks, indexing, or traffic from an SEO recommendation.

faq.question: What data does this skill use?
faq.answer: It can use Search Console, analytics, live-page checks, crawl results, and configured keyword or backlink providers.

faq.question: Can it edit my website?
faq.answer: Its documented tools return evidence rather than editing pages. The instructions require the assistant to ask before making page edits.

faq.question: Does it guarantee better rankings?
faq.answer: No. It identifies evidence and opportunities, but search performance depends on many external factors.

faq.question: Can it investigate a traffic drop?
faq.answer: Yes. Compare periods around the suspected date, inspect affected pages, and check indexing and live-page evidence.

faq.question: Can it perform keyword research?
faq.answer: Yes, when a supported research provider is configured. Results may be estimated, capped, filtered, or incomplete.

faq.question: What setup do Claude, Codex, and Claude Code need?
faq.answer: Connect the SEO MCP service or install the SEO CLI after reviewing its source and permissions. Crawls and internal-link analysis require local tools.
